newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Garuda sees potential in air cargo.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Garuda sees potential in air cargo.

text.p: Indonesia's national airline Garuda said on Monday it was committed to further investment in the air cargo sector after launching its first cargo flight at the weekend, and was confident of growth potential in the market.

Garuda on Sunday unveiled its first plane dedicated to cargo services. Part of a new and separate cargo division, the Boeing 737-200C will serve domestic routes in eastern Indonesia and operate from the country's second largest city, Surabaya, a Garuda official told Reuters.
A second plane, which will begin operations next week, will serve western Indonesia and be based on Batam Island, 20 km (12 miles) south of Singapore, said the official, who asked not to be named.
"Garuda has a commitment to cargo and that is why we set up a special division," he said. "We see business cargo as having great potential and not just in Indonesia."

The two planes, leased from Malaysia Airline Systems Bhd (MAS), a unit of Malaysia Airlines, will carry cargo from distribution centres in Batam and Surabaya to Jakarta's International Sukarno-Hatta airport.
But the official said Garuda was also bullish about the long-term growth prospects of the international air freight business and the airline planned future expansion in the sector.
"Our target for the share of cargo in the future total revenue of Garuda is 17 to 18 percent. This is our target for cargo within one year," he said.
Despite recent falling cargo rates and plunging yields in the world cargo business, the official said Garuda still saw growth potential.

"We see Japan, America and Europe as all good markets for cargo," the official said, adding that the airline was currently negotiating to join the German national carrier Deutsche Lufthansa in serving European markets from Batam.

He said that Garuda's international passenger operations were currently limited to joint ventures. The airline flies once a week to Los Angeles via Taipei with China Airlines and two times a week to Seoul with Korean Air Lines.

Earlier this year, Indonesia moved to protect domestic cargo carriers by limiting foreign operators to Hang Nadim airport on Batam Island. The government has said it wants to develop Batam into an international cargo hub to rival Singapore's Changi airport.
